🗄️ Database Health & Reconciliation
Compares Netlify DB vs Supabase bucket-by-bucket. Neither database can directly query the other — this endpoint brokers the check.
Click Check Now to compare both databases.
Bucket Status Netlify Rows Supabase Rows Netlify Updated Supabase Updated
📋 Evaluation Rules
48-Hour Evaluation Cooldown
By default, a 48-hour wait is enforced between consecutive evaluations of the same agent (Admins can still override individually while this is active). Toggle this OFF to lift the rule system-wide — all users (QA, TL, Admin) can evaluate any agent at any time without a confirmation prompt. All evaluations are still recorded in the change history.
Note: This setting takes effect immediately across all active sessions. Use with caution — lifting the cooldown allows back-to-back evaluations which may skew QA metrics. Restore the rule when batch evaluation is no longer needed.
🚀 Data Migration & Integration Hub
Export all QMS data, schema, and business logic. Deploy to any on-prem Windows Server, cloud provider, or integrate with AI agents and MCP servers. This production instance runs a dual-database backend (Netlify Postgres + Supabase mirror) — exports pull the merged view from /api/data.
📦 Full Data Export
Pulls all buckets — users, agents, evaluations, NPS, settings, and form config — into a single signed JSON bundle ready to import anywhere.
🧠 Business Logic Export
Exports QA form structure, scoring rules, pass thresholds, role permissions, and system settings as a portable config — survives any infrastructure move.
🗄️ Database Schema (DDL)
Ready-to-run SQL — paste into your database admin tool and execute before importing data. PostgreSQL includes the row-level merge function this instance already uses server-side.

      
    

  


  
  

    
🎯 Push to Target Server

    

      Point to any server that implements the same /api/data GET + POST contract. All buckets are pushed with the merge strategy — no data is overwritten.
    

    

      
      
      
    

    

    

      
Migration log:

      

    

  


  
  

    
📥 Import Bundle

    

      Upload a previously exported JSON bundle and push it to the current backend or a custom target URL.
      The merge strategy is applied — existing records are never overwritten.
    

    

      
      
    

    

  


  
  

    
📡 On-Prem Server Package

    

      Drop-in Node.js server that speaks the same /api/data contract as this production instance. Runs on Windows Server, Linux, or any Docker container.
      Uses SQLite by default (zero config) — swap to PostgreSQL or SQL Server via environment variables.
    

    

      

        
Quick start (Windows Server)

        node --version   # need v18+
npm install
node server.js   # listens on :3001
      

      

        
Environment variables

        PORT=3001
DB_TYPE=sqlite|postgres|mssql
DB_URL=./qms.db  # or connection string
CORS_ORIGIN=https://yourdomain.com
      

    

    

      
      
      
      
    

  


  
  

    
🤖 AI & MCP Integration

    

      QMS exposes a simple REST API that any AI agent or MCP server can call. Download the OpenAPI spec or the MCP server stub to connect Claude, GPT, or any LLM tool.
    

    

      

        
Endpoints available to AI

        

          GET  /api/data → all buckets (merged across both DB mirrors)

          POST /api/data → upsert bucket

          POST /api/auth → issue a session token

          GET  /api/reconcile → dual-database drift report

          All responses are JSON arrays with id fields — LLM-friendly.
        

      

      

        
MCP server stub

        

          The stub exposes get_data, push_data, and query_records as MCP tools — ready for Claude Desktop or any MCP client.
